messages:
tara: Quick thread: we need an autoscale policy framework for Dedicated that operators can reason about. Customers keep asking for deterministic behavior + an easy rollback if prewarm/autoscale misfires.
henry: Agree. Current ask from Finance/Sales: show predictable cost, predictable tail latency, and a safe escape hatch.
ops-oncall: Ops requirements: explicit rollout windows, kill-switch, and observable decision-path for every autoscale action. We need the policy to emit WHY it scaled (rule_id + inputs).
sales-liz: For contracts, customers want a clause: if prewarm fails to meet SLA for X windows, they get a credit. That needs deterministic measurement.
infra-lead: Proposal: define a policy DSL and a runtime decision trace. Policy example below. We store every decision as DECISION_TRACE event with fields: rule_id, inputs, score, action_taken, fallback_action, correlation_id.

```
autoscale_policy:
  name: slo_first
  target_slo_ms: 120
  rules:
    - id: ramp_up_node
      when: predicted_p90 > target_slo_ms and burst_credit_pct >= 5
      action: prewarm_nodes(count=2, reserve=true)
      fallback: increase_batch_size
      cooldown: 600
    - id: conserve_cost
      when: predicted_qps < baseline * 0.5
      action: scale_down_nodes(min=reserved)
      cooldown: 1800
```

tara: DSL should be versioned. Default policy = slo_first for enterprise, cost_first for trials. Also, add a per-tenant opt-out for prewarm.
henry: We must define deterministic measurement for SLA: measure tail latency on requests that hit a prewarmed node only, with labels to correlate reservation_id. Credit calculation hooks to billing.
ops-oncall: Rollback mechanics: - automatic rollback after N failed prewarm attempts in M minutes - manual kill-switch in Console + API - tenant-level circuit breaker. Also require a canary roll: apply policy to 1% traffic for 15m, evaluate, then ramp.
infra-lead: Decision trace example (stringified JSON stored in events): {rule_id: "ramp_up_node", inputs: {...}, score: 0.87, action: "prewarm_nodes:2", fallback: "increase_batch_size"} — this will make debugging much easier.
sales-liz: For customer-facing SLA: we need a transparent metric: prewarm_success_rate and a monthly credit formula: credit = surcharge_paid * (1 - success_rate). Finance wants the formula upfront.
tara: Launch checklist idea: 1) Policy DSL v1 + schema + Console policy editor; 2) DECISION_TRACE event and 90d retention in OLAP; 3) Billing hook: reservation_id + decision_trace correlation; 4) Canary runner + automatic rollback; 5) Docs + legal SLA wording.
ops-oncall: Observability: dashboard with live decision traces, prewarm_health by region, and an alert if decision traceback latency > 5s (means runtime slowdowns).
henry: Prioritization: spike to build DECISION_TRACE + minimal DSL parser (1wk). Then 2 sprints to integrate with prewarm runtime, Console editor, and billing tags. Can we staff 3 engs for the next 4 weeks?
infra-lead: Yes, asking for 2 runtime, 1 infra for the spike. We'll need an ops runbook for rollback and a test harness for canaries.
tara: Decision: run spike. I'll draft the policy PR template and the customer SLA draft. Assign owners: henry (policy DSL), infra-lead (decision trace + events), ops-oncall (runbook & canary).
product-bot: Created tickets: #PL-4300 (spike: autoscale policy trace), #ENG-4555 (DSL parser), #OPS-1522 (rollback runbook), #BILL-2420 (billing correlation).
henry: I'll put up a short RFC with examples and a minimal console mock by EOD Friday.
tara: Thanks everyone. Follow-ups: ops-oncall please sketch the canary gating conditions, infra-lead publish the DECISION_TRACE schema in repo, henry add DSL grammar to RFC.
